transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… it’s mostly that I keep checking things. Boxes, lists, drawers in the condo… I’ll look, and then I’ll go back and look again, even when I know I already did. My wife’s usually waiting for me to just leave it alone, but I have a hard time moving on.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to stop thinking about them?

Yes… I suppose so. I get these nagging thoughts that maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. I’ll tell myself it’s probably fine, but then the thought comes back anyway, and it’s hard to settle.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Not a certain number, no. It’s more that I keep feeling I have to look again — the same boxes, lists, drawers — before I can let it go. Even when I know I already checked, I still end up going back. My wife’s usually waiting, and I know I should just leave it be.
Are you checking these things because you're afraid something bad will happen if you don't?

Not exactly something bad, no… it’s more that I can’t seem to move on until I’ve checked again. Boxes, lists, drawers at the condo. I know I already looked, and my wife is waiting, but I still feel pulled back to it.
Do you feel like there's a right or wrong way to do these checks?

I don’t know that there’s a “right” way, exactly. It’s more… I feel like I haven’t really finished until I’ve gone back through the same boxes, the lists, the condo drawers. Even though I know I already checked. My wife will be waiting, and I still have trouble just leaving it alone.
Are you checking these things because you're trying to prevent something from happening?

No… I don’t think it’s to prevent anything, exactly. It’s just that I can’t move on until I’ve checked the same boxes, lists, and drawers again, even though I know I already did. My wife’s waiting, and I still… I still feel like I have to look.
Do you feel less anxious after you've checked these things again?

A little, maybe. Mostly I just feel like I can finally move on once I’ve looked again… even though I know I already checked the boxes or the lists or the drawers. It doesn’t last, exactly, but it lets me leave it alone for the moment.
Do you feel like the things you're checking need to be in a specific order or arranged in a certain way?

Not really arranged, no. It’s more that I keep going back to the same boxes, lists, and drawers before I can let it go. I know I already looked, and my wife is waiting, but I still feel like I have to check again.
Do you feel like the things you're checking or arranging need to be symmetrical or perfect in some way?

No… not symmetrical or perfect, exactly. It’s more that I keep checking the same boxes, lists, and the condo drawers before I can move on, even though I know I already looked. My wife will be waiting, and I still have trouble just leaving it alone.
Do you feel like checking these things again is to prevent something bad from happening to yourself or others?

Not really… I don’t think it’s that something terrible will happen. It’s more I just can’t seem to move on until I’ve checked the same boxes or lists or drawers again, even when I know I already did and my wife is waiting.
Do you feel like checking these things helps you feel more in control?

Maybe a little, yes. It’s not a big dramatic thing… I just feel like I can’t move on until I’ve checked the same boxes or lists or the condo drawers again, even though I know I already looked. Then I can leave it alone, at least for a bit.
Do you think you're checking these things because you're afraid of making a mistake?

Yes… I suppose that’s closer. I get these nagging thoughts that maybe I threw away something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. I can tell myself it’s probably fine, but the thought comes back, and then it’s hard to settle.
Is your need to check things again mostly because you're worried about making a mistake or because it helps you feel more in control of the situation?
I’d say it’s more the mistake part, I suppose. I keep checking the same boxes or lists or drawers, even though I know I already looked. I just can’t quite leave it alone and move on.
Is your need to check things again mostly because you're trying to avoid making a mistake?

Yes, mostly. I keep thinking I might’ve missed something in a box, or a list, or one of the condo drawers. I know I already checked, but I don’t feel I can move on until I look again… even when my wife is waiting for me to just let it be.
Are you ever worried that something you touch might be contaminated?
Not really, no. I mean, I try to be reasonably clean, but I can’t say I’m especially worried that things I touch are contaminated.
Do you ever worry that if you don't check something, it could lead to harm to yourself or someone else?

Not harm, exactly. It’s more… I get this nagging thought that I might’ve thrown out something important from my old teaching files, or put a tool in the wrong box. I tell myself it’s probably fine, but the thought comes back and I have trouble settling unless I check.
Do you feel like the things you're checking need to be perfect or just that you don't want to miss something?

More that I don’t want to miss something, I’d say. It’s not about perfect exactly… I just get stuck thinking maybe I threw away an important teaching paper or put a tool in the wrong box. Even if I know it’s probably unlikely, it keeps coming back.
Do you feel like you're checking things to make sure they're in the right place or that everything is as it should be?

Yes… more that everything has to be where I think it is. I’ll check the same boxes, lists, or drawers in the condo again and again before I can move on. I know I already looked, but it doesn’t quite let go, and my wife is usually waiting for me to leave it alone.
Is your need to check things again more about avoiding mistakes or feeling in control of your surroundings?

I suppose it’s more about not missing a mistake. I don’t know if I’d call it control, exactly. I just keep going back to the same boxes, lists, drawers in the condo… even when I know I already checked. My wife is usually waiting for me to just stop, but it’s hard to move on.
Is your need to check things again driven by a fear that something is not exactly as it should be?

Yes… I suppose that’s part of it. I keep checking the same boxes, lists, drawers in the condo, even though I know I already looked. I just can’t quite move on, and my wife is usually waiting for me to leave it be.
